title: Discrete nonempty generization fibres of strict localization
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $x,y\in X$ with $x\in\overline{\{y\}}$, and let $\bar x$ be a geometric point over $x$ [def-weil-geometric-point]. The canonical strict-localization morphism $X_{(\bar x)}\to X$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit, def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map] has discrete fibres. Its fibre over $y$ is nonempty.

source.place: Expose XIV, Proposition 2.1.4 proof (the strict-localization map is pro-etale/flat with discrete fibres)

proof.text: Choose an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ containing $x$ from a Noetherian affine cover of $X$, and write $\mathfrak p$ for the prime of $x$. Let $H$ be the coordinate ring of $X_{(\bar x)}$. In [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-ring-triples], take $Y=X$ and the chosen $U$. Its initiality and diagram equivalence identify $H$ with the filtered colimit of the etale $A$-algebras in the residue-triple category for $(A,\mathfrak p,K)$, where $K$ is the separable closure of $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ inside the field of $\bar x$. Use the small representatives fixed in [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]; passing to the corresponding equivalent diagram of triples keeps its index small and filtered. The structural maps $A\to B\to H$ agree by the cocone equations; call their common value $b:A\to H$. Since the neighbourhoods over $U$ have the same colimit and the comparison preserves their legs, the structural map factors as $\operatorname{Spec}H\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Spec}b}U\hookrightarrow X$. In particular its fibres outside $U$ are empty.

source.place: Tag 04HX (lemma-describe-etale-local-ring), affine neighbourhood and triple-colimit comparison

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-etale-triples-localized-strict-henselization] to the universal triple cocone of Step 1, its comparison with $H$, and $b$. This gives a compatible $A_{\mathfrak p}$-algebra structure on $H$, with $A\to A_{\mathfrak p}\to H=b$, and makes $H$ the algebraic strict henselization of $A_{\mathfrak p}$ relative to a separable closure of its residue field. Write $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak pA_{\mathfrak p}$ and $L$ for this separable closure. The pair category of [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization] for $(A_{\mathfrak p},L)$ is isomorphic to the triple category of [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples] for $(A_{\mathfrak p},\mathfrak m,L)$, compatibly with the forgetful diagrams: an $A_{\mathfrak p}$-algebra map $\chi:S\to L$ has prime kernel $\mathfrak q$, which lies over $\mathfrak m$ because $A_{\mathfrak p}\to L$ factors through the residue field, and $\chi$ induces a $\kappa(\mathfrak m)$-algebra map $\phi:\kappa(\mathfrak q)\to L$; conversely $(S,\mathfrak q,\phi)$ gives $\chi=S\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)\xrightarrow{\phi}L$, and the two morphism conditions $\chi'\circ\beta=\chi$ and $\beta^{-1}(\mathfrak q')=\mathfrak q,\ \phi'\circ\kappa(\beta)=\phi$ agree. Hence $H$ is $A_{\mathfrak p}$-isomorphic to the colimit $(A_{\mathfrak p})^{\mathrm{sh}}$ of that lemma, the strict henselization meant in [lem-sc-strict-henselization-noetherian] and in the faithful-flatness lemma of Step 6, and Noetherianity and faithful flatness transfer along this isomorphism. The ring $A_{\mathfrak p}$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian], since $A$ is Noetherian and we localize at $A\setminus\mathfrak p$. Hence [lem-sc-strict-henselization-noetherian] shows that $H$ is Noetherian. The explicit prime $\mathfrak p$ here is the prime of $x$, not an unspecified prime supplied by an existential local-presentation assertion.

source.place: Tag 06LJ (lemma-henselization-noetherian); algebra.tex Tag 04GW (lemma-strict-henselization-different) for the compatible local-base presentation; algebra.tex Tag 04GW again for the pair/triple description of $(R_{\mathfrak p})^{sh}$ at the maximal ideal

proof.text: For any $z\in U$, let $\mathfrak r\subset A$ be its prime and put $C=\kappa(\mathfrak r)\otimes_A H$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-etale-fiber-structure] to the small filtered diagram of etale $A$-algebras obtained in Step 1. It says that every prime of $C$ is maximal, so $\operatorname{Spec}C$ has dimension at most zero. No finite-type hypothesis on $A\to H$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 0AH1 (lemma-filtered-colimit-etale-noetherian-fibres), proof: no nontrivial specializations in the fibre

proof.text: The fibre ring has the concrete presentation $C\simeq S^{-1}(H/\mathfrak rH)$, where $S$ is the image of $A\setminus\mathfrak r$. The maps send $\bar h/s$ to $s^{-1}\otimes h$ and $a/t\otimes h$ to $\overline{b(a)h}/b(t)$; the fraction and tensor relations make them well-defined and their composites fix the displayed generators. The quotient $H/\mathfrak rH$ is Noetherian directly: lift an ideal to an ideal of $H$, take finitely many generators there, and take their images. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] its localization $C$ is Noetherian. This includes the zero ring and the case that the localization kills the quotient.

source.place: Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence), quotient argument in the proof and localization assertion

proof.text: By Steps 3 and 4, $\operatorname{Spec}C$ is a Noetherian scheme of dimension at most zero (its single affine chart has Noetherian ring). Thus [lem-sc-zero-dim-noetherian-finite-discrete] makes its underlying space finite and discrete. The tensor-factor exchange $\lambda\otimes h\mapsto h\otimes\lambda$, with inverse given by the same formula, identifies $C$ with $H\otimes_A\kappa(\mathfrak r)$. Now [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-spec-homeomorphism] identifies this spectrum homeomorphically with the topological fibre of $\operatorname{Spec}b$ over $z$. Consequently that fibre is discrete. Step 1 identifies it with the fibre in $X$, and gives empty, hence discrete, fibres outside $U$. This proves discreteness of every fibre.

source.place: Tag 0AAX (lemma-locally-Noetherian-dimension-0); algebra.tex Tag 00E6 (remark-fundamental-diagram) for the fibre homeomorphism

proof.text: Since $x\in\overline{\{y\}}$, the open set $U$ containing $x$ also contains $y$. Write $\mathfrak r$ for the prime of $y$ in $A$. The Zariski closure condition says $\mathfrak r\subseteq\mathfrak p$: the closure of the point $\mathfrak r$ is $V(\mathfrak r)$. Therefore $\mathfrak r$ avoids $A\setminus\mathfrak p$ and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-spectrum-embedding] supplies a prime $\mathfrak r_{\mathfrak p}$ of $A_{\mathfrak p}$ contracting to $\mathfrak r$. By the identification in Step 2, [lem-sc-strict-henselization-faithfully-flat] makes $A_{\mathfrak p}\to H$ faithfully flat. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-surjective-spectrum] to obtain a prime $Q\subset H$ over $\mathfrak r_{\mathfrak p}$. The equality $A\to A_{\mathfrak p}\to H=b$ implies $b^{-1}(Q)=\mathfrak r$. Hence $Q$ is a point of the fibre over $y$, proving nonemptiness, also when $y=x$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q54-d1cd87cd5 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all 15 cited statements, ILO XIV 2.1.3–2.1.4 (pp. 209–210) and Stacks 0AH1, 06LJ and 04GW. No SGA source is used. The statement is true and unchanged apart from the added reference to the structural-map node. I checked it on a field, the closed point of a Noetherian curve, fibres outside U, y=x, a nonreduced X, and A² at the origin with y the generic point of a line. There are no new nodes and no duplicate or cycle. Steps 1 and 3–6 match the cited statements. The ind-étale fibre is zero-dimensional without Noetherianity, the fibre ring S⁻¹(H/rH) is Noetherian (elementary step), the fibre is finite and discrete, and nonemptiness follows from r⊆p, faithful flatness over A_p and b⁻¹(Q)=r. One fault (C3/C4) is fixed. Step 2 gets H as a strict henselization in the sense of def-sc-ring-strict-henselization (the category of pairs), but lem-sc-strict-henselization-noetherian and, in Step 6, lem-sc-strict-henselization-faithfully-flat are about the triple colimit of lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples. The step never connected the two. The fix adds the pair↔triple isomorphism at the maximal ideal of A_p (ker χ lies over m; φ gives χ; the morphism conditions agree) and the A_p-isomorphism of H with that colimit. It cites both nodes in Step 2 and proof_deps, and adds a tool_uses entry for the triples lemma. I accept the other generic tool_uses: the triples comparison, the sbc localized henselization, the sc Noetherian and faithfully-flat lemmas, the filtered-étale fibre lemma and the zero-dimensional Noetherian lemma.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
